newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB liquidity injections not inflationary - Meyer.
newsitem.headline: SNB liquidity injections not inflationary - Meyer.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank's recent injections of liquidity were not seen likely to fuel inflation, said Swiss National Bank president Hans Meyer.
"Inflation is not an acute problem," said Meyer, speaking to a Swiss television crew after a speech here.

He was responding to a question about the implications of the SNB's latest liquidity additions after the SNB said last week it would aggressively add liquidity to the banking system to counter the Swiss franc's rise.

In a speech earlier on Tuesday, Meyer noted the Swiss economy currently is growing well below the roughly 2.00 percent per annum rate which it can sustain over a long term without endangering price stability.
"Our economy can grow for a longer period by nearly 2.00 percent per year, without overburdening production capacity, and thus leading to noticeable inflationary pressure," he said in the speech.
